title: heuristic-driven-block-prefetch-and-deferred-pinning-orchestrator
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a heuristic-driven prefetch orchestrator and deferred pinning strategy for paged KV to reduce tail-latency and improve throughput; opt-in via runtime flag; rollout with canary and A/B split.
commits: feat: add prefetch_orchestrator with pluggable heuristics (prefetch_orchestrator.{cc,h})
perf: integrate heuristics into paged_block_manager hot-paths and introduce async hinting
feat: deferred_pin_queue implementation and background flusher
test: unit + integration tests and canary config
body:
Motivation: The paged KV block manager suffers intermittent tail latency spikes during sudden sequence-length increases and bursty workloads. Existing eager pinning keeps frequently accessed blocks resident but creates contention on the pin manager and increases eviction jitter under heavy batch churn. This PR introduces a heuristic-driven prefetch orchestrator combined with a deferred pinning queue to smooth pin/evict ops and proactively warm likely-needed blocks without blocking critical request paths.

Design summary: The prefetch orchestrator runs in the background and subscribes to access summaries emitted by the PagedBlockManager. It evaluates short-window heuristics (recency-weighted hit streaks, inter-arrival distribution, sequence-length projection) and issues async prefetch hints to the block manager. Hints are low-priority and can be coalesced. The deferred_pin_queue accepts pin requests from hot-paths annotated as "defer-eligible"; pins are batched and committed during low-util windows or when pinned-set pressure crosses a threshold. The orchestrator and queue are feature-flagged and tunable via runtime_flags.proto.

Key changes: Added prefetch_orchestrator.{cc,h} implementing a pluggable HeuristicEngine with three built-in strategies (short-term burst predictor, semantic repeat detector, and cold-start estimator). Integrated async hint path into paged_block_manager.cc to accept hint tokens that avoid immediate locking in the critical RPC path. Implemented deferred_pin_queue with a bounded ring buffer, background flusher, and backpressure signals for the scheduler. Exposed metrics: kv_prefetch.hints_issued, kv_prefetch.hits_from_hint, kv_prefetch.prefetch_latency_ms, kv_pin.deferred_batch_size, kv_pin.deferred_flush_count, kv_pin.flush_backpressure.

Performance: Canary tests against a synthetic chat workload with mixed short/long sequences show: p95 generation latency reduced by 18% on average under 2x burst load, throughput increase of 12% due to fewer synchronous pin stalls, and a 26% reduction in eviction churn measured by evict ops/sec. Memory overhead: steady-state pinned-set unchanged (+~1.2% due to conservative prefetch TTL).

Testing: Unit tests added for heuristic behaviors and deferred queue semantics. Integration canary described in services/serving/kv/tests/integration/paged_kv_prefetch_canary.yaml. CI initially showed a transient flake in sched/evict_test; rerun green. Load canary ran for 24h in staging with two canary hosts (5% traffic) before merge.

Rollout plan: Feature gated off by default. Rollout steps: 1) merge behind runtime flag; 2) enable for 5% traffic in staging canary and run 24h; 3) incrementally increase to 25/50% while observing kv_prefetch.* and kv_pin.* metrics; 4) enable in main if no regressions for 72h. We will also add a runtime fast-fail path to disable prefetching entirely if kv_prefetch.hits_from_hint < 5% for a sustained period.

Backward compatibility: No public API change. Runtime flags added are optional. Behavior of pinned-set is conservative by default.

Observability: Added dashboards and alert rules in docs/observability/kv-prefetch-metrics.md. Key alerts: sustained prefetch miss rate, deferred_pin backlog > threshold, and flush_backpressure > threshold.

Review notes and tradeoffs: - Heuristic selection intentionally conservative to avoid over-prefetching; future work includes a lightweight online learner to tune thresholds. - Deferred pinning can delay first-use latency for very hot blocks if misclassified; mitigations include an inverted fast-path that forces immediate pin when request latency is already degraded. - We prioritized minimal locking on RPC hot-paths, moving heavier work to background threads; correctness validated with stress tests.

Review conversation (high level): Diego Ruiz: "Please add a short doc that explains the heuristic tuning knobs and their operational profiles; also add an opt-out metric for on-call to be able to disable prefetch quickly." Author: "Added docs & metrics and a runtime kill-switch flag; included in this PR." Samir Kothari: "Concern about ring buffer overflow during extreme bursts." Author: "Implemented bounded ring + oldest-drop policy and added backpressure metric for scheduler to throttle producers." Lena Hwang: "Can we add an integration test that simulates long tail growth?" Author: "Added a stress scenario in paged_kv_prefetch_canary.yaml and extended integration tests to validate no deadlocks under 10k concurrent hint producers."

Merge notes: After two approving reviews and green CI, merged with squash. Canary run and staging observations met success criteria.

Files of interest (high level): - services/serving/kv/paged_block_manager.cc: adds async hint consumer, light-weight hint token structure, and hook points for deferred_pin_queue. - services/serving/kv/prefetch_orchestrator.cc: new background orchestrator and HeuristicEngine implementations. - services/serving/kv/deferred_pin_queue.cc: batched pin commit logic and backpressure controls. - docs/: updated operational playbook and dashboard definitions.

If you want to test locally: build //services/serving:kv and run //services/serving/kv/tests:prefetch_orchestrator_test; to run the canary locally use the yaml under tests/integration with the staging harness.

Related work/items: ENG-2489 (KV tail-latency program), ENG-2510 (paging scheduler improvements).
